intro.title: Fulgurite Fusion
intro.text:
Harness the storm.

This guide follows the mod from your first lightning strike to the Fusion Reactor.

Power in this mod is Fulmen (Fm). You make it from fuel, store it in batteries, send it down wires and use it to run machines, colliders and finally a fusion reactor.

Pick a chapter on the right, or turn the pages with the arrows, the arrow keys or the mouse wheel.

pages.title: Glass made by lightning
pages.text:
When lightning strikes sand, it fuses a vein of Raw Fulgurite down into the ground.

A lightning rod standing on a block passes its strike to the block below it, so a rod on sand grows fulgurite on demand. Stand rods on sand and wait for a thunderstorm.

pages.title: Mining it
pages.text:
Mine Raw Fulgurite for 4-8 Fulgurite Shards (Silk Touch gives the block itself).

Nine shards craft into two Fulgurite, the mod's main material.

pages.title: Fulmen (Fm)
pages.text:
Fm is the mod's power. Generators push it into machines touching them, batteries store it, and wires carry it between Machine Connectors.

Rates are in Fm per tick (Fm/t); there are 20 ticks in a second.

pages.title: Your first generator
pages.text:
Strike a vanilla furnace with lightning (a lightning rod on top works) and it becomes a Weak Storm Furnace.

It burns fuel into Fm and pushes it into machines touching any face except its front.

pages.title: Fuel
pages.text:
Every fuel is worth a fixed amount of Fm: one coal is 5,120 Fm. Other fuels scale with how long they burn in a normal furnace.

Higher tiers don't get more out of a fuel, they deliver it faster:
 Weak: 16 Fm/t
 Enhanced: 32 Fm/t
 Charged: 64 Fm/t

pages.title: Grounding
pages.text:
An ungrounded Storm Furnace builds up static and shocks players nearby. The shock gets stronger with each tier.

Ground it with three lightning rods stacked straight down under the furnace. Its menu shows whether it's grounded.

pages.title: Upgrade ritual
pages.text:
Lightning upgrades a Storm Furnace one tier if the right offerings are in place. Blocks go against all four side faces; items are dropped on top.

Weak to Enhanced: 4 copper blocks, 2 Charged Spark Cells, 1 diamond.

Enhanced to Charged: 4 gold blocks, 6 Charged Spark Cells, 6 netherite ingots.

If anything is missing, nothing upgrades, and the lightning will likely burn your offering.

pages.title: Bottled power
pages.text: Empty Spark Cells hold a little Fm. They're used in recipes, the ritual and the colliders.

pages.title: Fulgurite Charger
pages.text:
Charges Empty Spark Cells: 1,280 Fm each, drawing 16 Fm/t (4 seconds a cell).

It passes power on to machines touching it, so it can sit in a daisy chain.

pages.title: Stronger cells
pages.text:
Charged and Overcharged Spark Cells are made in the Storm Collider:

Spark Cell + Redstone Block = Charged Spark Cell

Charged Spark Cell + Arc Core = Overcharged Spark Cell

pages.title: Storm Battery
pages.text:
Holds 64,000 Fm. Power comes in on any face and goes out to any touching machine.

Touching batteries form a bank (up to 6) that fills and drains as one, with one big gauge across the whole bank.

pages.title: Machine Connector
pages.text:
Sticks to any face of any block, like a torch.

On a machine it links that machine to a wire network. On a plain block (fence, wall, log) it's a relay, so you can build power poles. On a multiblock machine only the power port takes one.

Right-click it with an empty hand to see the network's status.

pages.title: Wires
pages.text:
Wire Rolls string hanging wires between connectors: use the roll on one connector, then the next.

Raw Wire: 16 blocks. Bare copper: carrying power, it shocks creatures in water nearby.
Insulated Wire: 16 blocks, safe.
Heavy Wire: 32 blocks.

A network can feed up to 8 machines.

pages.title: Daisy chains
pages.text:
Machines touching each other pass power along, in any mix of types. A chain stops after 8 machines.

Batteries don't pass power through chains; they feed what they touch.

pages.title: Converters
pages.text:
FE Converter: Fm in, Forge Energy out of the front (1 Fm = 10 FE).

Universal EU Converter: Fm in on any side, EU out of the front. It matches the voltage of the GregTech or Modern Industrialization cable or machine on its front.

pages.title: Multiblock machines
pages.text:
Each machine is a cube of Arc Casings with a controller on the front face, bottom row.

Small (2x2x2): Press, Arc Furnace, Wire Extruder. The controller is at the front-left bottom.

Large (3x3x3): Kiln, Crusher. The controller is at the front-centre bottom.

pages.title: Arc Casings
pages.text:
A machine runs at the tier of its lowest casing. Each tier runs twice as fast as the one before:
 Crude 1x, Tempered 2x, Charged 4x, Prime 8x.

pages.title: Ports
pages.text:
Power port: top layer, at the back. A Machine Connector goes on it.

Input port: top layer, at the front. A hopper above fills the machine.

Output port: bottom layer, at the back. A hopper below (or a pipe beside) empties it.

Right-click any part of the machine to open its menu.

pages.title: What they make
pages.text:
Press: ingots into Copper, Iron and Gold Sheets.

Wire Extruder: a Copper Sheet into 2 Raw Wire.

Kiln: 2 Fulgurite into a Coil Segment.

Arc Furnace: anything a furnace smelts.

Crusher: raw ore into 2 crushed ore (smelt it into ingots).

pages.title: The collider ring
pages.text:
A 7x7 ring, one layer, with the collider block in the middle:

 21 Fulgurite Ring blocks round the edge
 1 Collider Input in the middle of one side
 2 Collider Injectors in the middle of the two sides next to it
 the fourth side's middle is a ring block

pages.title: A shot
pages.text:
Two Spark Cells leave the input in opposite directions, run one full lap of the ring, then carry on to the first injector they reach, which fires them into the middle to collide.

In the Mini Collider each collision releases 5,120 Fm over 40 seconds. Power comes out of the top: a machine or battery on top, or a Machine Connector.

Right-click any part of the ring for its menu.

pages.title: Pairing machine
pages.text:
Swap the Storm Collider in for the Mini Collider and the ring becomes a pairing machine.

Each injector holds one material; every shot carries one from each into the middle and the pair decides the result. It costs 10,000 Fm a shot, fed from any side or a connector on top.

Products come out of the bottom into a hopper or pipe, or sneak + right-click to take them.

pages.title: Crafting pairs
pages.text:
Fulgurite + Fulgurite = Refined Fulgurite

Prime Spark Fragment + Prime Spark Fragment = Prime Spark

Spark Cell + Redstone Block = Charged Spark Cell

Charged Spark Cell + Arc Core = Overcharged Spark Cell

pages.title: Fusion Fuel
pages.text:
Pair two exotic materials and the collision makes a Fusion Fuel capsule for the Fusion Reactor, sometimes with a byproduct.

This is the safe way to find out what a pairing does: bad results here only shock, smoke or knock back. They never break blocks.

pages.title: The twelve
pages.text:
Twelve rare materials, each with its own energy. Any two can be paired, 78 pairings in all, and each has its own result.

The Stormwing Plume comes from Stormwings.

pages.title: Pairing results
pages.text:
Fizzle: no reaction, wasted.
Steady: reliable power.
Strong: lots of power.
Jackpot: huge power, sometimes a rare byproduct.
Unstable: big but spiky; shocks.
Bad: poor power, smoke and harm.
Catastrophic: an explosion, and in the reactor, real damage.
Wildcard: Struck Spore pairings roll a different result each time.

pages.title: Learning them
pages.text: Pairings you've made are remembered, so you learn which are safe. Try new pairings in the Storm Collider first: there, a bad result can't wreck anything.

pages.title: Storm eagles
pages.text:
Great storm birds that nest on the high peaks: jagged, frozen and stony.

In clear or rainy weather they sit calmly on their nests. In a thunderstorm they circle and attack any player they see, and once they fight you they don't give up.

Hurt and angry, they dive with lightning.

pages.title: Plumes and guards
pages.text:
Hitting a Stormwing can shake loose a Stormwing Plume.

A bird sitting on its nest sheds Molted Plumes into the bowl now and then.

Every so often a Stormwing flies off to hunt. While it's away an Arc Serpent guards the nest.

pages.title: Storm Caller
pages.text:
Hold right-click for 2 seconds to call a thunderstorm (5 minutes). It costs a Charged Spark Cell, and only works from clear skies under open sky.

Any thunderstorm wakes the Stormwings up.

pages.title: Eggs
pages.text:
About one nest in ten holds a Stormwing Egg.

An egg only warms beside a running Storm Collider, and hatches after 20-40 minutes of it. Whatever the collider fires while the egg warms shapes the bird inside, and risky pairings can hatch something wild.

pages.title: Hatchlings
pages.text:
A hatchling can't fly yet: it walks, leaps and glides. It grows up after one Minecraft day.

A loyal hatchling follows the player who placed the egg. Right-click it with an empty hand to make it stay or follow; it keeps that when it grows up. A grown loyal bird follows you, sits on command and defends you.

A feral one runs from everyone and grows into a dangerous bird.

pages.title: Overview
pages.text:
The Fusion Reactor fires two fuels round two huge rings and smashes them together in a blast chamber, for enormous amounts of Fm.

It has four parts: the blast chamber with the Fusion Collider in its middle, the inner ring, the outer ring and the control console.

Every part is explosion-proof. Right-click the Fusion Collider to see what's missing.

pages.title: Blast chamber
pages.text:
A hollow 5x5x5 cube with the Fusion Collider in the very middle.

Edges: Blast Chamber Frame. Faces: Fulgurite Blast Glass. Leave the middle block of two opposite side faces open (east and west, or north and south): that's where the beams come in.

Once it's right it forms on its own into an armoured sphere with portholes.

pages.title: The ring tubes
pages.text:
Both rings are the same diamond-shaped tube running round a square channel: glass at the four tips (top, bottom, inside, outside), Reinforced Fulgurite on the four diagonals, and air down the middle.

The inner ring's channel is 9 blocks out from the collider, the outer ring's 44 blocks out.

When everything is right the tubes form into smooth glowing rings.

pages.title: Inner ring parts
pages.text:
Two Fusion Injectors on the inner ring's inside face, 7 blocks out from the collider, in line with the chamber's open faces, fronts facing the chamber.

Two Receiver Portals on its outside face, at opposite corners, at the end of a straight side.

pages.title: Outer ring parts
pages.text:
Two Transfer Portals on the outer ring's inside face, each straight in line with a Receiver Portal. The charge jumps across the open air between them, so keep that gap clear.

Two Ring Injection Ports on the outside face at one corner, each in line with the channel of the other side. They replace the middle outer glass there.

pages.title: Control console
pages.text:
7 wide, 3 tall, 1 deep. Place the Reactor Control Console (control panel) first, facing you, in the middle of the middle row. Seen from the front:

Top: casings all along.
Middle: Power Port, casing, casing, CONTROL PANEL, casing, casing, Power Port.
Bottom: casing, Fuel Input, Data Port, casing, Data Port, Fuel Input, casing.

Once formed, the casings turn into the frame, power gauge, displays and fuel screens.

pages.title: Data cables
pages.text:
Run a Data Cable from each Console Data Port to a Ring Injection Port, one cable per port. The left port carries fuel 1, the right fuel 2. Keep the two cables apart, and each under 128 blocks.

The cable is a free-standing metal pipe with smooth bends.

The rings only form once both cables are connected.

pages.title: Fuel
pages.text:
Each fuel slot takes a Fusion Fuel capsule or a raw exotic material. Load them in the console's menu, or with hoppers or pipes into the Fuel Inputs from the front or back.

Two capsules: both capsules' power added, then doubled. The best.
Two raw materials: their pairing's normal power.
One of each: in between.

pages.title: A run
pages.text:
Each run needs an 8,000 Fm startup charge. The console takes it from a battery or generator behind a power port.

Press Start (or turn Auto on). The two charges fire from the Ring Injection Ports and race opposite ways round the outer ring for 6 laps, 30 seconds, speeding up all the way.

They jump from the Transfer Portals to the Receiver Portals, scream through 6 laps of the inner ring, and are fired into the chamber to collide.

pages.title: Power out
pages.text:
The collision's Fm fills the console's store (2,000,000 Fm). The power ports push it out of their backs, 2,048 Fm/t each, into a battery or machine behind them.

The menu shows the store, the run's progress and the last result.

pages.title: When it goes wrong
pages.text:
A cut data cable: that injector gets no fuel. The other charge fires anyway, finds nothing to hit, and is lost.

Something in a portal beam's path: that charge fizzles out.

Unstable, Bad and Catastrophic fuels unleash shocks, smoke, withering or an explosion. A Catastrophic run also blasts several ring and chamber blocks out, and the reactor stays down until you replace them.

A lost run turns Auto off.
